title_en: Supplementary Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Current Handling of Theft Cases
keywords_en: theft; Procuratorate's Opinion on Current Handling of Theft Cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate

Supplementary Notice on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Current Handling of Theft Cases

Fa (Yan) Fa [1986] No. 26

The High People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Courts and Military Procuratorates; the Railway Transport High Court; and the National Railway Transport Procuratorate:

According to reports from many localities, in recent years, some thieves who have previously received administrative or criminal punishment for theft on several occasions have again engaged in activities such as picking locks and pickpocketing. In such cases, the amount of theft found is sometimes not large, but the impact on disrupting social order is very harmful. In order to promptly and strictly handle such cases, it is hereby decided: Paragraph (2) of Article 5 of the (84) Fa Yan Zi No. 14 "Interpretation on Several Questions Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Current Handling of Theft Cases", which originally read: "... those who have previously received administrative or criminal punishment for theft on several occasions and repeatedly steal or pickpocket, where the amount is not large, may be subjected to re-education through labor; those whose household registration is in the countryside but who commit crimes in cities and towns may also be subjected to re-education through labor," is hereby amended to read: "... those who have previously received administrative or criminal punishment for theft on several occasions and again steal or pickpocket, where the amount is not large, may be subjected to re-education through labor; those whose household registration is in the countryside but who commit crimes in cities and towns may also be subjected to re-education through labor; where individual circumstances are egregious and constitute a crime, criminal liability may also be pursued according to law."

September 17, 1986
